text.en: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living organisms.
Prokaryotic cells keep their genetic material inside a well-defined nucleus.

modelCorrection.en: Prokaryotic cells have no well-defined nucleus. Their genetic material is in a region called the nucleoid.

text.en: All cells are surrounded by a cell membrane.
Cells of plants and animals both have a cell wall outside the membrane.

modelCorrection.en: Cells of plants, fungi and bacteria have a cell wall. Animal cells do not.

text.en: Meiosis produces four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes.
Mitosis produces two daughter cells with half the DNA of the parent cell.

modelCorrection.en: Mitosis produces two daughter cells identical to the parent cell.
